prompt: The script uses querySelector to find the first .price element.
why: JavaScript looks up elements in the DOM, the tree the browser built from the HTML.
trap: Changing it would be the next step; this is finding it.

prompt: Clicking a list item lets the code walk up to its parent ul.
tells: walk up to its parent ul
why: Elements have parents and children in the DOM tree.
trap: The click starts it, but moving through the tree is the DOM.

prompt: The Elements panel shows the page as a tree you can expand and collapse.
tells: shows the page as a tree
why: That tree is the DOM: the browser's live model of the page.
trap: It came from HTML, but what you see is the live tree.

prompt: View Source shows the original HTML, but the Elements panel shows items JavaScript added later.
why: The DOM is the live page, which can differ from the source file.
trap: JavaScript changed it, but the clue is the difference between source and tree.

prompt: The code counts how many child elements the menu contains.
tells: how many child elements the menu contains
why: Reading an element's children uses the DOM tree.
trap: Nothing changes yet; it's reading the tree.

prompt: Each element in JavaScript is an object with properties like textContent and className.
tells: an object with properties like textContent
why: The DOM represents elements as objects JavaScript can work with.
trap: Setting them would be changing the page; the clue is what they are.
